clue.text: Item used to clear up skin initially shed

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word skin

parts.note: a shed and a hovel are both rough, simple outbuildings

explanation.surface: Something used to tidy away skin that has been shed, like a snake's cast-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a verb about skin; it is the noun, a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A spade-like tool is the thing you scoop up mess or snow with when clearing.

clue.text: Superior-sounding business that's clear, like glass

indicators.note: sounding says the word for superior is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: superior means higher, placed above
a line is a line of business, a trade

explanation.surface: A posh-sounding firm whose dealings are transparent as glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical term for something glassy and translucent, from the Greek for glass.

clue.text: Weaknesses of spokespersons lacking love

indicators.note: lacking means the following item is missing from the spokespersons word

parts.note: voices are those who speak for a group
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: The failings of press officers who have no affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Vices are moral failings or bad habits, character flaws.

clue.text: The French maidens must be bowled over by him

parts.note: la is a French word for the

indicators.note: bowled over means knocked down and tumbled, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Young women are bound to be swept off their feet by this charmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maidens' suggests cricket's maiden overs alongside 'bowled'; here it is just the word to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's man, who sweeps women off their feet, is a womaniser or charmer.

clue.text: Surveillance post abroad

parts.note: a stake is a post driven into the ground
abroad can mean out and about, outside

explanation.surface: A monitoring station sited overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Police watching a place covertly over time are on a watch operation of this kind.

clue.text: Views welcoming the rise of Brown in legislative assemblies

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so one word holds the other

parts.note: views as a verb means sees

indicators.note: in a down clue, rise means the word reads upward, backwards

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Parliaments with opinions that embrace the ascent of a politician named Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a person's name; it is the colour, read upward because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper houses such as the US and Roman ones are lawmaking chambers.

clue.text: Jelly babies at last seen in a short film

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film

indicators.note: at last asks for the final letter of the babies word

explanation.surface: Jelly Babies, the sweets, finally appear in a brief movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jelly babies' reads as the British sweet; the definition is just 'Jelly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury gelatine made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Clear old flame on Ecstasy charge

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a rate is a price or fee

explanation.surface: Acquit a former lover facing a drugs charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone of blame is to absolve or acquit them formally.

clue.text: Can opener, for example, let us in free?

indicators.note: free signals the letters are released and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tin-opener asks whether it may release us.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin-opener is one kind of kitchen tool or implement.

clue.text: Intricately connected pair liable to suffer a mishap

indicators.note: intricately suggests something tangled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Two linked items, complexly joined, that tend to go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who often has mishaps is said to be clumsy and susceptible to them.

clue.text: Girl with fur, with some dodgy characters?

parts.note: miss is a young girl
a pelt is an animal's fur skin

explanation.surface: A young woman in a fur coat keeping shady company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' are letters, not people: a word with dodgy letters is wrongly spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongly written word contains letters that are wrong, punningly dodgy characters.

clue.text: Stop crossing right line for a batsman

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so one word sits across the other

parts.note: cease means stop

explanation.surface: Instructions not to step over the line in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the white line marking where the batsman stands.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the marked line in front of the stumps that a batter must stay behind.

clue.text: Soldiers in favour of mass change for the better

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
for means in favour of
m is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Troops backing a large movement for improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve something or someone by amending faults; to mend one's ways.

clue.text: Unfashionable editor supporting drama excelled in game

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed below the other piece

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A dated editor backing a play outshone the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat an opponent by playing better is to outperform them in a match.

clue.text: Developed as well as tidal barriers

indicators.note: developed means grown into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Coastal defences that were built up too.
explanation.definitionFit: Embankments built along a coast hold back the sea and its tides.

clue.text: Firepower needed where there's trouble in vessel

indicators.note: in places the trouble word inside the vessel word

parts.note: an artery is a blood vessel
ill means trouble or harm

explanation.surface: Big guns are called for where there is strife aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship; it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy guns and cannons give an army its firepower.

clue.text: Gut feeling that's vague, when the DI goes missing

indicators.note: goes missing means those two letters vanish from the word for vague

parts.note: indistinct means vague, unclear

explanation.surface: A hunch that is fuzzy once the detective inspector has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is a detective inspector in the surface, but here just the two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An intuition or innate impulse is a feeling in the gut.

clue.text: No mountain in South Africa is worthy of mention!

parts.note: Table Mountain overlooks Cape Town in South Africa

explanation.surface: Claims that no South African peak deserves comment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noteworthy or remarkable deserves to be mentioned.

clue.text: Experienced in love? Quite the reverse, getting burnt!

indicators.note: in says one piece sits within the other
quite the reverse flips the containment: love goes inside the experienced word, not around it

parts.note: tasted means experienced, as in tasted success
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they know love, but it is the other way round and they get scorched.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread that is browned under heat is lightly scorched.

clue.text: Paces studies, on time

indicators.note: on means placed after, the studies word following the time letter

parts.note: reads means studies, as at university

explanation.surface: Someone walks about the study, punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk or step steadily is to tread, so paces and treads are synonyms.

clue.text: Prescribed act, accepting European credit

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the act word holds the other letters

parts.note: a deed is an act

explanation.surface: A legislated act that takes in European credit rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ordered by authority has been laid down or prescribed.

clue.text: Almost nicked identity, showing no emotion

indicators.note: almost means the word for nicked loses its final letter

parts.note: nicked is British slang for stole
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: An identity thief caught short, remaining poker-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: Impassive and unemotional, calm and dull in temperament.

clue.text: Wild animal shot after loud noise

indicators.note: after means the shot word follows the noise word

parts.note: a din is a loud noise
a shot is a go, an attempt

explanation.surface: A wild beast is gunned down following a bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests gunfire; it means an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild dog of Australia is an untamed animal.

clue.text: Union of a couple of students making a nice change

parts.note: L for learner stands for a student, so two of them give two Ls

indicators.note: change signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two students marrying and making a pleasant difference.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact or league joining parties together is a union of them.

clue.text: A military establishment put to shame

parts.note: a base is a military establishment

explanation.surface: An army camp brought into disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: To humble or degrade someone is to lower their dignity, shaming them.

clue.text: Unacceptable, but past help, ate out

parts.note: beyond means past

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Bad behaviour from someone who dined out, past saving.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for conduct outside accepted bounds of decency.

clue.text: Lumber that is of no use to employer

definitions.meaning: dead branches and timber, wood that has died on the tree

definitions.text: that is of no use to employer
definitions.meaning: staff who contribute nothing to a firm and could be cut

explanation.surface: Timber that is useless to the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally dead timber; figuratively useless staff or members dragging an organisation down.

clue.text: Submits financial returns

definitions.meaning: the income an investment produces, as in dividend payouts

explanation.surface: Someone hands in their tax figures.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means surrenders; as a noun, the returns produced by investments.
